say: Growth marketing asks a wider question. Of everyone who heard about us, how many became happy, paying, returning customers who brought friends? It treats the journey as one system, finds the weakest point, and fixes it with small, measured experiments.

say: A business can double its sales without spending more on adverts, if it stops losing people after they arrive.

say: Every customer passes through five stages, nicknamed pirate metrics because the initials spell AARRR. Acquisition: how do people find you? Activation: do they have a good first experience, like a first order?

Revenue: do we make money from them?

say: Retention: do they come back, say within 30 days? Referral: do they bring others?

say: Revenue: do you make money from them? For each stage, use the same month, and count people, not actions. One customer who sends five messages is one chat, not five.

say: Each step rate is that stage divided by the stage before it. The best target is a low rate with a cheap fix, not simply the smallest number.

say: Numbers show where people leave. Conversations show why. Ada reads 30 chats that did not convert. Most asked about delivery days and never got a clear reply. A quick reply with menu, prices and delivery schedule is her cheap first experiment.

say: Growth that loses money on every customer is not growth. For example, Chioma sells shea-butter skincare from Ibadan. Last month she spent 150,000 naira on Instagram ads and won 50 new customers.
Customer acquisition cost, or CAC, is spend divided by new customers from that channel: 3,000 naira each.
Her average order is 10,000 naira with a 40 percent margin, so each order earns 4,000 naira gross profit. Customers buy about 3 times a year, so lifetime value, or LTV, is 12,000 naira.
That is 4 to 1, and her first order already pays back the CAC. She can scale carefully, watching CAC every week.

Use gross profit, not revenue, for LTV. Calculate CAC for each channel separately. Use only the period you can actually observe. And when you scale, raise spend in steps, for example 20 to 30% per week.

panel.heading: Honest numbers vs flattering numbers
left: Use the period you can observe
right: Divide all spend by all customers

say: Using revenue can make a loss-making channel look healthy. Mixing channels hides a bad one behind a good one. And CAC often climbs when you double the budget, so recalculate each time.

say: Many Nigerian customers pay per megabyte, prefer transfer or pay-on-delivery, and have been burned by fake vendors. So the first lever is trust: customer videos, a trial size, a verified payment page, and fast replies.

cards.d: Show proof early, offer a low-risk first step, use a verified checkout link, reply fast.
Light pages, compressed images, a WhatsApp catalogue, short voice notes.
K = invites per customer x share who buy. Reward only after the friend pays.

say: The second lever is respect for data costs. Every heavy page or long video costs your customer money before she has bought anything.

cards.d: Show proof early, offer a low-risk first step, use a verified checkout link, reply fast.
Light pages, compressed images, a WhatsApp catalogue, short voice notes.
K = invites per customer x share who buy. Reward only after the friend pays.

say: The third is a referral loop. For example, Funmi's tutoring parents each share an invite with 2 others, and 15% enrol. K is 0.3, so 100 parents bring about 43 extra, at 2,000 naira each, less than half her ad CAC of 4,500 naira.

say: Pay referral rewards only after the new customer's payment clears, and cap rewards per person, so nobody invents fake accounts or refers herself with a second number.

panel.heading: Protect customers and your budget
items: Pay rewards only after payment clears
Never ask for OTPs, PINs or card details
Say publicly that you never will

say: Never ask customers for OTPs, PINs or card details on WhatsApp, and tell them publicly that you never will, because scammers copy popular referral offers.

say: To remember. Measure all five stages. Fix the leak with a clear cause and a cheap fix. Check LTV to CAC and payback for each channel. And check retention before you pour money into ads, or you fill a bucket with a hole in it.

Pick the leak with a clear, cheap fix
LTV = order x margin x orders
